MATHEMATICS: correct, verified by hand step by step; finite I is essential (the support-union identity fails for infinite I); d = 0 is harmless. APPLICATION: valid -- with f = fiveState, d = sixty, fiveState_adj supplies the premise for non-adjacent pairs and five_support_step_ban for adjacent ones, so it proves five_support_no_sixty. DEPENDENCY AUDIT (the decisive finding): strict_state_no_unit_support has TWO direct users, not one -- five_support_no_sixty (FiveSupport:138) and interfaceStateSupport_no_unit (Interfaces:266) -- and 24 transitive users including no_proper_five_coloring. verified_results: GRADE [M] The Astra joint-pair lemma is TRUE as stated: {f=i} = disjoint union_j Q_ij; S_i = union_j supp(volume|Q_ij) using restrict-additivity over a finite disjoint family and support of a finite measure sum; pick j with a in supp Q_ij; translation invariance of Lebesgue measure plus openness of t -> t+d gives a+d in S_j; if a+d in S_i then the contact premise makes Q_ij null, so its restricted measure is zero and its support empty, contradicting a's membership.

GRADE [M] The finite index hypothesis is ESSENTIAL, not a convenience: for infinite I a countable union of null joint-pair sets can carry full measure, so the support-union identity fails. d = 0 is harmless (the premise then forces the support empty).

GRADE [M] The application is valid: at iota = Fin 5, f t = fiveState c hc x (t : Angles), d = sixty, the joint-pair set is exactly {t | fiveState t = i and fiveState (t+sixty) = j}; fiveState_adj (Accumulation:390) gives the premise for non-adjacent pairs after pulling back along angleMk_quasiMeasurePreserving, and five_support_step_ban (FiveSupport:91) gives it for adjacent pairs whose supports meet. Conclusion a in fiveSupport i implies a+sixty not in fiveSupport i is exactly five_support_no_sixty (FiveSupport:138).

GRADE [C] DECISIVE DEPENDENCY FINDING: strict_state_no_unit_support (States:704) has exactly two direct users -- five_support_no_sixty (FiveSupport.lean:138) and interfaceStateSupport_no_unit (Interfaces.lean:266). Its transitive user set has 24 declarations, including interfaceStateSupport_margin, four_interface_word_data, no_four_interfaces, commonInterface_graph_acyclic, five_sequence_no_accumulation, cyclicCore_compact_finite, fullApprox_exists, no_measurable_weak_five_coloring, no_proper_five_coloring_algebraic and no_proper_five_coloring itself.

GRADE [C] Therefore the proposal removes ONE OF TWO uses and does not delete strict_state_no_unit_support from the development; the Interfaces/CyclicCore/FullApproximation chain still needs it for the main theorem. Net cost is +100 to +150 lines against ~4 deleted lines, with no theorem removed. This is NOT a simplification and must not be described as a Lemma 6.7 deletion (manuscript naming unresolved, and on this evidence no deletion occurs).

GRADE [P] Delivered ONE minimal Lean module jointpair/JointPairSupport.lean (117 lines) stating the generic theorem over real Lebesgue measure with Fintype iota and Measurable f, reusing the development's own stateSupport (FiveSupport:38). It is a PLAN: three named blockers B1 (restrict of a finite disjoint union), B2 (support of a finite sum), B3 (translate of a support point), each with candidate Mathlib names, plus a caveat that the closing proof's rewrites are unchecked. No admission tactic appears; the blockers are undefined constants so the file cannot compile and cannot be mistaken for a proof.
GRADE [P] Exact replacement proof of five_support_no_sixty sketched in section 4 of the audit with the two premise cases and the retained/dropped lemma list.

conjectures: The Astra route would become a genuine simplification only if interfaceStateSupport_no_unit and its 24-descendant chain could also be rerouted to a support-based argument; no evidence for that exists, and it is a much larger project than the one lemma.

Conversely, if the joint-pair lemma is proved, it is a reusable finite-to-infinite support tool in its own right and may help elsewhere; that is a separate claim from removing strict_state_no_unit_support.
The three blockers are library-shape questions, not mathematical ones; B1 and B2 are the likely 4.35 breakages.
